'''David A. W. Hutchinson''' (born 1969) is a [[quantum physics|quantum physicist]] and professor in [[Department_of_Physics_at_the_University_of_Otago|Department of Physics]] at the [[University of Otago]], Dunedin, New Zealand. He was the inaugural director of the [[Dodd-Walls Centre|Dodd-Walls Centre for Photonic and Quantum Technologies]], a New Zealand government-funded national [[Centre of Research Excellence (New Zealand)|Centre of Research Excellence]]. He served as director from the centre's inception in January 2015 through to the end of March 2023. Hutchinson's research interests are in the areas of [[quantum biology]], [[Bose–Einstein condensate|Bose-Einstein condensates]], and the underlying mathematics of quantum physics.

== Biography ==
Born in England in 1969, Hutchinson completed a BSc at the [[University of Exeter]], UK, and received a PhD degree there in 1994 in the area of theoretical physics.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|last=Gibb|first=John|date=5 February 2015|title=It's all happening for physicist|work=[[Otago Daily Times]] |url=https://www.odt.co.nz/news/dunedin/its-all-happening-physicist|access-date=2020-05-05}}</ref> Whilst at Exeter he was awarded [[Sporting colours|half colours]] in 1992 for "excellence in student sport".<ref name=":colours">{{Cite web|title=Awards and Colours|url=https://sport.exeter.ac.uk/media/universityofexeter/campusservices/sport/documents/Awards_and_Colours_Spreadsheet.xlsx|website=University of Exeter|access-date=2024-04-29}}</ref> He also holds a PGDip (Arts) in philosophy from the University of Otago.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=David Hutchinson|url=https://www.otago.ac.nz/physics/staff/DavidHutchinson.html|website=University of Otago – Department of Physics|access-date=2020-05-05}}</ref>

He moved to New Zealand in 2000, and became a full citizen in February 2015.<ref name=":3" /> Hutchinson is currently chair of the board at Otago Museum,<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|title=About the Museum → Trust Board Members → David Hutchinson|url=https://otagomuseum.nz/about/news/ |access-date=2024-04-20}}</ref> and was a departmental science advisor for New Zealand's [[Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment]] from 2021 - 2024.

== Academic career ==
Hutchinson held [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral research]] fellowships at [[Dublin City University]], Ireland, and then at [[Queen's University at Kingston]], Ontario.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|last=Gibb|first=John|date=1 November 2008|title=Let's get physical|page=62|work=[[Otago Daily Times]] }}</ref> He was lecturer in physics at [[Somerville College]], [[University of Oxford]] in the UK from 1997 to 2000.<ref name=":1" /> After visiting the [[University of Otago]], [[Dunedin]], New Zealand during a [[Royal Society|Royal Society of London]] Study Visit in 1998, he moved to Dunedin in 2000 to take up a lectureship position at the university.<ref name=":1" /> He was promoted to senior lecturer in 2003, then associate professor, and in February 2015 became a full professor.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1" /> In 2004 he was the first recipient of Otago University's Rowheath Trust Award and Carl Smith Medal,<ref name=":">{{Cite web|title=The Rowheath Trust Award and Carl Smith Medal|url=https://www.otago.ac.nz/research/awards#the-rowheath-trust-award-and-carl-smith-medal|website=University of Otago|access-date=2024-04-22}}</ref> for outstanding research performance by an early-career researcher.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite news|last=Gibb|first=John|date=27 September 2008|title=Outstanding Otago scientist joins champions in China|work=[[Otago Daily Times]] |url=https://www.odt.co.nz/news/campus/university-of-otago/outstanding-otago-scientist-joins-champions-china|access-date=2020-05-05}}</ref> He attended the annual [[World Economic Forum]] "Meeting of New Champions" in [[Tianjin]] (2008) and Dalian (2009), selected as "one of the world's 60 outstanding young scientists"; the attendees went on to form the [[Global Young Academy]] in Berlin in 2010, of which Hutchinson is an alumnus.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Gibb|first=John|date=30 September 2009|title=Mentor visit to China lifts NZ's physics profile|work=[[Otago Daily Times]] |url=https://www.odt.co.nz/news/dunedin/mentor-visit-china-lifts-nzs-physics-profile|access-date=2020-05-05}}</ref><ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Brück|first1=Tilman|last2=Beaudry|first2=Catherine|last3=Hilgenkamp|first3=Hans|last4=Karoonuthaisiri|first4=Nitsara|last5=Mohamed|first5=Hiba Salah-Eldin|last6=Weiss|first6=Gregory A.|date=2010-04-02|title=Empowering Young Scientists|journal=Science|volume=328|issue=5974|pages=17|doi=10.1126/science.1185745|issn=0036-8075|pmid=20360070|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Hutchinson was a member of the Jack Dodd Centre for Quantum Technology at Otago's [[Department_of_Physics_at_the_University_of_Otago|Department of Physics]], and served as the director from 2010 to 2015, except for a period in 2012 when he was a visiting professor at the [[Centre for Quantum Technologies]] at the [[National University of Singapore]]. In 2018 Hutchinson was visiting fellow at [[Merton College]] at the [[University of Oxford]], an opportunity given to just a handful of educators around the world per year.

On 1 January 2015 he became director of the newly founded [[Dodd-Walls Centre for Photonic and Quantum Technologies]], a [[Centre of Research Excellence]] (CoRE).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Let There Be Light - The Dodd-Walls Centre|url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/national/programmes/ourchangingworld/audio/20167552/let-there-be-light-the-dodd-walls-centre|date=2015-02-17|website=[[RNZ]] |access-date=2020-05-05}}</ref> Hosted by the University of Otago, the Dodd-Walls centre is composed of approximately 200 researchers and students from six New Zealand universities: Otago University, the University of Auckland, [[Victoria University of Wellington]], [[Auckland University of Technology|AUT]], [[Massey University]], and the [[University of Canterbury]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=About Us|url=https://doddwalls.ac.nz/about/|website=The Dodd-Walls Centre|access-date=2020-05-05}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Gibb|first=John|date=24 November 2014|title=Quantum leap for university research|work=[[Otago Daily Times]] |url=https://www.odt.co.nz/news/dunedin/quantum-leap-university-research|access-date=2020-05-05}}</ref>

Hutchinson is a passionate practitioner of education outreach, giving regular talks in schools and community organisations. In 2017 he was one of a team of science educators, including [[Ian P. Griffin|Ian Griffin]], who visited the [[Chatham Islands]] to work with school pupils.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Gibb|first=John|date=22 July 2017|title=Science educators off to Chathams|work=[[Otago Daily Times]] |url=https://www.odt.co.nz/news/dunedin/science-educators-chathams|access-date=2020-05-05}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Taking science to the extremes|url=https://www.curiousminds.nz/stories/taking-science-to-the-extremes/|date=2017-10-19|website=Curious Minds, He Hihiri i te Mahara|access-date=2020-05-05}}</ref> He has participated in several [[marae]]-based Science Wānanga and worked with the Lab in a Box programme around New Zealand.

During his time with Lab in a Box, Hutchinson attended [[Polyfest]] in 2020 with the [[Dodd-Walls Centre]], connecting with Pasifika students.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Research group hopes to win fans to science at Polyfest|url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/programmes/datelinepacific/audio/2018737999/research-group-hopes-to-win-fans-to-science-at-polyfest|date=2020-03-11|website=[[RNZ]] |access-date=2020-05-05}}</ref> He also attended the New Zealand LUMA Light Festival in 2018 in a similar capacity, with more than 2,000 people struck by the Lab in a Box attraction.<ref>{{Cite web|title=DWC at NZ LUMA Festival 2018|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qKoQxXn1nwc|date=2018-08-24|website=YouTube|access-date=2024-04-22}}</ref>

Hutchinson has worked at the intersection of art and science as an outreach tool, working at both an organisational level and as a practitioner. An example of this was a mural he commissioned from Dunedin artist [[Bruce Mahalski]] during his time as director at the Dodd Walls Centre in 2022. The mural used ultraviolet light-reactive paint to bring the art alive at night.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Glow in the dark outdoor mural unveiled in Dunedin|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A4JTqhROpDE|date=2022-02-03|website=TVNZ on YouTube|access-date=2024-04-22}}</ref> Hutchinson is also part of the shortlisting panel for [[Quantum Shorts]], a science-based flash-fiction writing competition.

He has been a member of the Trust Board of the [[Otago Museum]] since 2008 and took over as chair of the board after the death of Graham Crombie in 2019.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news|last=Gibb|first=John|date=21 February 2019|title=Send-off given to 'larger than life character'|work=[[Otago Daily Times]] |url=https://www.odt.co.nz/news/dunedin/send-given-larger-life-character|access-date=2020-05-05}}</ref> He is a fellow and past president of the [[New Zealand Institute of Physics]], and former president of the Otago Institute, the [[Royal Society Te Apārangi]]'s Otago-Southland branch.<ref>{{citation |url=http://nzip.org.nz/about-nzip/nzip-fellows/ |title=NZIP Fellows |publisher=New Zealand Institute of Physics |access-date=5 July 2019}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> He is also an elected fellow of the UK's [[Institute of Physics]].<ref name=":0" />

In 2022 Hutchinson was awarded the Royal Society Te Apārangi's [[Thomson Medal (Royal Society of New Zealand)|Thomson Medal]], for "establishing and developing the Dodd-Walls Centre for Photonic and Quantum Technologies, advocating for early career researchers and developing outreach partnerships through the museum sector".<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Dunedin Study wins Rutherford Medal and other Research Honours Aotearoa winners celebrated in Ōtepoti Dunedin |url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/news/research-honours-aotearoa-winners-celebrated-in-otepoti-dunedin/ |access-date=2022-11-16 |website=Royal Society Te Apārangi}}</ref>

== Research ==
Hutchinson is a theoretical physicist, specialising in quantum systems and ultra-cold atomic gases.<ref name=":0" /> Specifically, he examines the effects of disorder in [[Bose–Einstein condensate]]s (systems first created in 1995, and at University of Otago since 1998, which form at close to [[absolute zero]]).<ref name=":1" /> He has also worked on understanding energy transport on the [[Fenna-Matthews-Olson complex|FMO complex]] found in deep-sea bacteria which rely on [[infrared]] [[photon]]s, and its possible implications for producing more efficient [[Photovoltaics|solar photovoltaic panels]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Quantum mechanics - do deep-sea bacteria do it?|url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/national/programmes/ourchangingworld/audio/201830499/quantum-mechanics-do-deep-sea-bacteria-do-it|date=2017-01-24|website=[[RNZ]] |access-date=2020-05-05}}</ref>
